bibl.title: Attentional sensitization of unconscious visual processing: Top-down influences on masked priming

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: According to this model, attentional influences originating from task sets enhance task-relevant unconscious processes while attenuating task-irrelevant unconscious processes.

span.label: subliminal masked priming
span.quote: In this article, we describe our attentional sensitization model and review recent evidence demonstrating attentional influences on subliminal priming, a prototypical example of an automatic process.

span.label: review
span.quote: In the upcoming two parts of this article, we will review latest evidence demonstrating a variety of attentional influences on several forms of unconscious priming.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Task representations raise the neuronal gain of task-relevant processing pathways and lower it in task-irrelevant ones, so unconscious stimuli are amplified or attenuated according to their congruence with the current task set
span.quote: Processing in task-relevant pathways is enhanced by increasing the gain of the neurons in the corresponding areas, whereas processing in task-irrelevant pathways is attenuated by a decrease of the gain ( Reynolds, Pasternak, & Desimone, 2000 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Prefrontal top-down signals adjust the sensitivity of posterior processing pathways to incoming sensory input, whether or not that input reaches awareness
span.quote: unconscious cognition is assumed to be controlled by top-down signals from prefrontal cortex ( Haynes et al., 2007 ) that increase or decrease the sensitivity of processing pathways for incoming sensory input

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Backward inhibition suppresses the just-abandoned task set while the next task is prepared, which reverses the direction of the sensitization effect at long intervals
span.quote: This result pattern is compatible with the notion of a backward inhibition mechanism that suppresses irrelevant task sets in preparation of the next task

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Attentional sensitization applies to unconscious and conscious stimuli alike, being blind to whether the stimulus is consciously perceived
span.quote: We thus assume that an attentional sensitizing mechanism gradually enhances and attenuates stimulus processing irrespective of whether the stimulus is consciously perceived or not

span.label: The model's central neural assumption, a prefrontal top-down signal modulating posterior pathway sensitivity, has not yet been tested in detail.
span.quote: The assumption of the attentional sensitization model that control of unconscious processes is exerted by a prefrontal top-down signal, which in turn influences the sensitivity of processing pathways in posterior brain areas, should be tested in more detail by means of fMRI and electrophysiological recording techniques.

span.label: The theory is not yet formally specified, so its predictions about the dynamics of attentional control remain imprecise.
span.quote: Finally, formal computational modeling of the proposed attentional sensitization mechanism (see e.g., Trapp, Schroll, & Hamker, 2012 ) is desirable to render our theory more precise and to derive further empirically testable predictions regarding the dynamics of attentional control of conscious and unconscious visual processing in various task domains.

span.label: The gain parameter of neural network models, together with attentional gain modulation observed in primate single-cell recordings, is imported as the computational mechanism of the psychological attentional sensitization model
span.quote: Gain is a parameter in neural network modeling, which influences the probability that a neuron fires at a given activation level ( Hamker, 2005 ).

span.label: automaticity
span.quote: Given that attention and task demands are frequently found to modulate behavioral and neurophysiological effects, it is difficult to identify processes that actually meet the classical criteria for automaticity. The apparent lack of processes that fully meet the criteria of automaticity renders the classical view of automaticity unsatisfactory

span.label: autonomous
span.quote: Classical theories of automaticity assume that automatic processes elicited by unconscious stimuli are autonomous and independent of higher-level cognitive influences. In contrast to these classical conceptions, we argue that automatic processing depends on attentional amplification of task-congruent processing pathways and propose an attentional sensitization model of unconscious visual processing

span.label: attentional sensitization
span.quote: we argue that automatic processing depends on attentional amplification of task-congruent processing pathways and propose an attentional sensitization model of unconscious visual processing: According to this model, unconscious visual processing is automatic in the sense that it is initiated without deliberate intention

span.label: top-down control
span.quote: However, automatic processing is susceptible to attentional top-down control and is only elicited if the cognitive system is configured accordingly. Thus, unconscious automatic processing and the notion of attentional control is not a contradiction as it has been previously thought

span.label: subliminal priming
span.quote: We show that subliminal priming (a) depends on attentional resources, (b) is susceptible to stimulus expectations, (c) is influenced by action intentions, and (d) is modulated by task sets. These data suggest that attention enhances or attenuates unconscious visual processes

span.label: task sets
span.quote: We show that subliminal priming (a) depends on attentional resources, (b) is susceptible to stimulus expectations, (c) is influenced by action intentions, and (d) is modulated by task sets. These data suggest that attention enhances or attenuates unconscious visual processes

span.label: attentional resources
span.quote: We show that subliminal priming (a) depends on attentional resources, (b) is susceptible to stimulus expectations, (c) is influenced by action intentions, and (d) is modulated by task sets. These data suggest that attention enhances or attenuates unconscious visual processes

span.label: automaticity, CLASSICAL - and the sense worth recording is the OPERATIONAL consequence rather than the phrasing: if automatic processes are autonomous, then a behavioural or neurophysiological effect `has to be INVARIANT in order to index a truly automatic process`. The definition dictates a test, the test is invariance, and invariance is what gets measured. A conceptual assumption turned into an experimental criterion
span.quote: Based upon the assumption that automatic processes are autonomous, a behavioral or neurophysiological effect has to be invariant in order to index a “truly automatic” process ( Pessoa, Kastner, & Ungerleider, 2003 ). Such operational definitions of automaticity , which are essentially influenced by the classical view

span.label: A DEFINITION REJECTED BECAUSE ITS EXTENSION IS EMPTY. Attention and task demands modulate nearly every effect that has been looked at, so `it is difficult to identify processes that actually meet the classical criteria` - and `the apparent lack of processes that fully meet the criteria of automaticity renders the classical view UNSATISFACTORY`. Not refuted by a counter-example: retired because nothing in the world satisfies it. That is a distinct way for a term to change and the corpus should be able to find the cases
span.quote: Given that attention and task demands are frequently found to modulate behavioral and neurophysiological effects, it is difficult to identify processes that actually meet the classical criteria for automaticity. The apparent lack of processes that fully meet the criteria of automaticity renders the classical view of automaticity unsatisfactory

span.label: automaticity, REVISED - the same word with one criterion removed: automatic now means `does not depend on conscious awareness` and `is initiated WITHOUT DELIBERATE INTENTION`, and no longer means unmodulable. The paper states the consequence explicitly - unconscious automatic processing and attentional control `is NOT A CONTRADICTION as it has been previously thought`. Two criteria kept, one dropped, and the dropped one is the one that was selecting nothing
span.quote: We propose that processing can occur automatically in the sense that it does not depend on conscious awareness and that it is initiated without deliberate intention. However, automatic processing is susceptible to attentional top-down control and is only elicited if the cognitive system is configured accordingly. Thus, unconscious automatic processing and the notion of attentional control is not a contradiction as it has been previously thought

span.label: subliminal priming used as the HARD CASE for a general claim about automaticity: it is the field's prototypical automatic process, so showing four separate top-down influences on it - attentional resources, stimulus expectations, action intentions, task sets - is an argument about automaticity in general rather than about priming. The corpus's central phenomenon serving as somebody else's test object
span.quote: We show that subliminal priming (a) depends on attentional resources, (b) is susceptible to stimulus expectations, (c) is influenced by action intentions, and (d) is modulated by task sets. These data suggest that attention enhances or attenuates unconscious visual processes

span.label: contradicts → classical theories of automaticity (Posner & Snyder, 1975; Schneider & Shiffrin, 1977)
span.quote: Hence, in contrast to classical theories of automaticity ( Posner & Snyder, 1975 ; Schneider & Shiffrin, 1977 ), automatic processes elicited by unconscious visual stimuli are under attentional control to some extent.

span.label: builds-on → Kiefer & Martens, 2010
span.quote: We have therefore recently developed the attentional sensitization model of unconscious cognition ( Kiefer & Martens, 2010 ) that aims at explaining the various influences of top-down attention on different forms of unconscious automatic processing.

span.label: attentional sensitization —contrasted-with→ autonomous
span.note: differs in: WHETHER AN UNCONSCIOUS PROCESS CAN BE REACHED FROM ABOVE - the classical account makes autonomy definitional, this one makes prior attentional configuration a PRECONDITION for the process running at all. Not a weaker version of the same claim: the direction of dependence is reversed · strength of the relation: 0.95 — THE PAPER'S ARGUMENT, and the abstract states both sides in one sentence pair - `In contrast to these classical conceptions`. Confidence 0.95.
span.quote: Classical theories of automaticity assume that automatic processes elicited by unconscious stimuli are autonomous and independent of higher-level cognitive influences. In contrast to these classical conceptions, we argue that automatic processing depends on attentional amplification of task-congruent processing pathways and propose an attentional sensitization model of unconscious visual processing

span.label: top-down control —causes→ subliminal priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — The direction is recorded as `increases` because the paper's own summary is `enhances OR attenuates` - attention moves the effect in either direction depending on congruence with the task set, which is the point. A `no-change` reading would be wrong and a purely positive one incomplete; the quote carries both words.
span.quote: Although the classical view of automaticity is prevailing and still dominates current research, evidence for attentional top-down control of unconscious visual processing has been accumulated during the last years. Several attentional manipulations have been shown to reliably modulate subliminal priming effects. This highlights the generality and robustness of attentional effects on unconscious visual processing

span.label: task sets —causes→ subliminal priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — One of the four enumerated influences, kept as its own edge because `what the participant is set up to do changes what an unseen stimulus does` is the concrete form of the configuration claim.
span.quote: We show that subliminal priming (a) depends on attentional resources, (b) is susceptible to stimulus expectations, (c) is influenced by action intentions, and (d) is modulated by task sets. These data suggest that attention enhances or attenuates unconscious visual processes

span.label: attentional resources —causes→ subliminal priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — The sharpest of the four against the classical view: a process that consumes attentional resources is not autonomous by anybody's definition.
span.quote: We show that subliminal priming (a) depends on attentional resources, (b) is susceptible to stimulus expectations, (c) is influenced by action intentions, and (d) is modulated by task sets. These data suggest that attention enhances or attenuates unconscious visual processes

span.label: A semantic induction task performed shortly before a masked prime enhanced subsequent subliminal semantic priming in both reaction time and N400, whereas a perceptual induction task attenuated it.
span.quote: At the short RPI, semantic priming effects on RT and N400 ERP component were obtained when a semantic task set was induced immediately before subliminal prime presentation, whereas a previously induced perceptual task set attenuated priming.

span.label: The pattern reversed at the long response-prime interval, with priming present after the perceptual but not the semantic induction task.
span.quote: At the long RPI, significant priming was found after the perceptual induction task, but not after the semantic task.

span.label: Semantic and visuo-motor priming were doubly dissociated by induction task type, with visuo-motor priming appearing only after the perceptual task.
span.quote: Visuo-motor priming, depending on access to visual shape information, was only observed after the perceptual but not after the semantic induction task.

span.label: Attentional sensitization operates even within the perceptual domain: only a shape induction task, not a colour one, produced occipito-parietal ERP priming.
span.quote: We found occipito-parietal ERP priming effects only subsequent to the shape induction task.

span.label: A phonological letter-classification induction task, which discourages word reading, abolished subsequent subliminal semantic priming.
span.quote: In the latter experiment, semantic priming effects were only observed following the semantic classification, but not following the phonological letter classification induction task.

span.label: attentional sensitization model of unconscious cognition
span.term: attentional sensitization model of unconscious cognition
span.quote: We have therefore recently developed the attentional sensitization model of unconscious cognition ( Kiefer & Martens, 2010 ) that aims at explaining the various influences of top-down attention on different forms of unconscious automatic processing.

span.label: gain
span.quote: Gain is a parameter in neural network modeling, which influences the probability that a neuron fires at a given activation level ( Hamker, 2005 ).

span.label: preemptive control
span.quote: In preemptive control , top-down influences are initiated in advance of stimulus pre-sentation.

span.label: reactive control
span.quote: Preemptive control can be exerted for both conscious and unconscious stimulus presentation, whereas only consciously perceived stimuli are susceptible to reactive control in response to ongoing or completed stimulus processing.

span.label: task set
span.quote: we define task sets as an adaptive configuration of the cognitive system which is necessary to efficiently perform a given task

span.label: conditional automaticity
span.quote: Given this dependency on the precise configuration of the cognitive system, one might as well speak of conditional automaticity ( Bargh, 1989 ; Logan, 1989 ).

span.label: masked visuo-motor response priming
span.quote: Masked visuo-motor response priming denotes faster responses to visual shape targets, when the masked prime (also a visual shape) indicates the same rather than a different response

span.label: masked semantic priming
span.quote: It denotes facilitation of a response to a target word, when it is preceded by a semantically related masked prime word (e.g., chair-table ).

span.label: N400 ERP component
span.quote: Semantic priming modulates the N400 ERP component, a negative deflection peaking at about 400 ms with a centro-parietal topography ( Kutas & Hillyard, 1980 ).

span.label: induction task paradigm
span.quote: In our induction task paradigm, prior to the masked priming procedure, participants were engaged in different induction tasks (e.g., semantic classification vs. perceptual classification) designed to induce a specific task set (e.g., semantic or perceptual task set).

span.label: type of induction task (semantic vs perceptual, phonological word vs phonological letter, shape vs colour)
span.term: type of induction task (semantic vs perceptual, phonological word vs phonological letter, shape vs colour)
span.quote: Across experiments, we systematically varied the type of induction task to specify the attentional mechanisms which enhance or attenuate unconscious processing.

span.label: response-prime interval (RPI) of 200 or 800 ms
span.quote: We varied the time interval (either 200 or 800 ms) between the response to the induction task and the onset of the prime (RPI) in order to obtain information on how the influence of the induction task on masked priming unfolds over time.

span.label: subliminal priming effect, measured as reaction time difference and N400 amplitude difference between related and unrelated pairs
span.term: subliminal priming effect, measured as reaction time difference and N400 amplitude difference between related and unrelated pairs
span.quote: In all experiments, subliminal priming effects were assessed with behavioral (shorter reaction time [RT] to semantically related than to unrelated prime target pairs) and ERP measures (larger amplitude of the N400 ERP component, an electrophysiological index of semantic processing, for semantically unrelated than for related prime-target pairs).

span.label: difficulty and verbal/non-verbal nature of the induction tasks
span.term: difficulty and verbal/non-verbal nature of the induction tasks
span.quote: Across experiments, the difficulty of the semantic and perceptual induction tasks as well as their verbal or non-verbal nature was systematically varied.

span.label: 200 or 800 ms — The two response-prime intervals between the induction-task response and masked prime onset, manipulated to track how the task set decays
span.quote: We varied the time interval (either 200 or 800 ms) between the response to the induction task and the onset of the prime (RPI) in order to obtain information on how the influence of the induction task on masked priming unfolds over time.

span.label: about 600 ms — Duration a task representation is claimed (from the task-switching literature) to remain active after task completion, motivating the choice of the two RPIs
span.quote: because the task switching literature suggests that a task representation is active for about 600 ms after task completion

span.label: 40 targets — Large target set size in the cited Kiesel et al. expectancy manipulation, contrasted with a small four-target set
span.quote: In one condition, target set size was large (40 targets) so that a variety of words from different semantic categories was expected.
